study type: Mixed-methods study (retrospective cohort analysis and prospective cross-sectional survey)
exposure: Pregnant women's knowledge levels regarding HIV
cohort: The study included data from 1866 deliveries and 150 pregnant women attending antenatal care in three rural health facilities in Northwest Cameroon.
finding: The overall prevalence of maternal HIV infection was 5.0%, and a significant proportion of pregnant women demonstrated inadequate knowledge regarding the periods of mother-to-child transmission and its prevention.
mod_finding: Only 60.5% of pregnant women correctly identified labour/delivery as a period of mother-to-child transmission of HIV.
cross-section timing: Pregnant women were recruited over a 1-month period while attending antenatal care.
